resolution.note: thread/start turns off hooks, plugins, apps and every MCP server; live first call 19,630 -> 18,954 input tokens, zero hook/MCP frames

title: Worker app-server threads start the operator's MCP servers and run the lead's Codex hooks
body:
Evidence (2026-11-08, #393 first live recording of codex-cli 0.167.0, deleted after review because it carried account data): every worker thread started the 5 MCP servers of the operator's Codex home (figma, asana, builder-vm, node_repl, krn) and ran 4 user hooks from ~/.codex/hooks.json ("KRN: loading the outco…") around each turn. The first model call of a two-line brief took 19,630 uncached input tokens (test/fixtures/codex-app-server/compact.rpc, first thread/tokenUsage/updated). A worker needs neither: the lead's hooks put lead context into a worker turn, and MCP tool schemas widen every call.
Acceptance: worker threads start no MCP server and run no user hook while keeping auth (a thread/start config override, or a worker Codex home holding only auth by reference, never a copied secret). Proof: a live run with mcpServer/startupStatus/updated, hook/started and hook/completed left out of the driver's opt-out list shows none of them, and the PR reports the first-call inputTokens of `KRN_LIVE=1 node scripts/live-worker.mjs --record` before and after.

2026-11-08 research (t-cz92be6): two mechanisms with evidence. (1) Per-thread or launch-level overrides: features.hooks=false, features.plugins=false, features.apps=false and mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false for every name from `codex mcp list --json`, built in one function used by both the spawn and the identity check; on 0.167.0 a launch-level `-c` with an unknown key exits 1, so the override list fails closed (findings CX1 in .krn/runs/lead/t3code-agentic/lanes/t3-codex-driver.md, RP-01 in .krn/runs/lead/external-patterns/lanes/ext-repos.md). (2) A private CODEX_HOME with auth.json and auth.lock symlinked to the operator's files and a minimal config without skills, plugins or MCP servers (RP-04, Every's compound-engineering skill-eval cell). t3code does not isolate: its shadow home isolates auth only and its app-server threads get the operator's MCP servers and hooks (t3-codex-driver.md, Answers). Proof idea: a recorded run, or the mock-provider test of t-m1jmgcv, shows zero hook/started and mcpServer/startupStatus/updated frames and a first-call input token count below the 19,630 in test/fixtures/codex-app-server/compact.rpc.
